scope: Independent full-primary-source review of judicial research batches 1 and 2
result: All 45 selected historical case summaries supported after source-owner corrections; no unresolved publication blocker in this bounded review.
method: Read all included official opinion texts in full, using cached original PDFs and their text extractions. Independent review was divided among readers; the lead directly read six cases and checked the reports for the remaining 39.

Verified judge identity and role, actual trial action versus reviewing-court reasoning, dates, disposition, paragraph references, and expressed limits. Search snippets and index matches did not substitute for decisions.
Matched source PDF hashes against researcher ledgers; checked exact canonical case-key coverage.
Source owners applied corrections; reviewers did not change production data or the source ledgers.

cases.notes: Read all fifteen pages, including majority and dissent. Caption identifies Kerry M. Kennedy; trial facts/rationale paragraphs 19-20 support one-year sentence and shared school/church property. cases.caseName: Lewis v. Illinois State Board of Elections
cases.notes: Read all six pages. Caption names Ward Kirby; paragraphs 8-10 support the August 14 dismissal and alternative preclusion grounds; paragraphs 14-21 affirm only on untimeliness/statutory jurisdiction. No merits resolution of fraud allegations.

Read all four pages. Caption names Ward-Kirby. Paragraph 5 supports the May 16 ballot-access ruling and explicitly missing transcript. Paragraphs 6-13 reverse, uphold board removal, and bar counting votes. August 2 opinion follows May 31 accelerated order.

Read all seven pages. Caption identifies Byrne. Paragraph 16 gives June 18, 2015 denial; paragraphs 21-31 confirm innocence finding, voluntary-causation issue, extra-record evidence without meaningful response, and erroneous State-misconduct requirement. Paragraphs 33-34 vacate and remand, without awarding a certificate. Precision correction verified: missing allegations of State misconduct, not a standalone no-misconduct finding.

Read all fourteen pages. Caption identifies Byrne. Paragraph 32 distinguishes original detention judge from later relief judge. Paragraphs 27-35 support continued-detention relief denial; paragraphs 39-48 affirm. This is not the initial detention judgment or a finding of guilt. Unknown exact relief-denial date correctly remains null.

Read all six pages. Caption identifies Kenworthy as judge on appeal, while initial-appearance court is separate. Paragraphs 12-14 describe later release denial and February 17 relief denial; paragraph 16 confines preserved issue to release conditions; paragraphs 17-21 affirm after de novo review. No finding of criminal guilt or ruling on cash-bail policy.

cases.caseName: American Steel Fabricators, Inc. v. K&K Iron Works, LLC
cases.notes: Cover identifies Nixon as the circuit judge; Mikva authored the appellate opinion with Walker and Tailor. Ledger correctly avoids attributing appellate authorship to Nixon. Paragraphs 10, 15 and 19-20 support dismissal with prejudice for lack of statutory authority to issue the section 34 demand; it was a section 2-615 sufficiency ruling, not a general standing determination. Paragraphs 35-42 explain the appellate lienor-status rationale without requiring perfection; paragraph 48 reserves the alternative interested-person theory. Paragraphs 50-51 reverse and remand. The ledger accurately distinguishes the circuit rationale and appellate disagreement.

Cover names Powell as circuit judge and McBride as appellate author with Howse and Ellis. The $300,000 damages figure came from a jury verdict; the selected judicial action concerns enforcement and rejecting a reduction, as the ledger says. Paragraphs 1-4 support full judgment enforcement and rejection of Song's 10%-liability argument. The separate contribution allocation did not reduce liability to the patient. Paragraphs 1, 4 and 8-12 support the emotional-versus-bodily-injury statutory distinction. Paragraphs 18-22 establish the contribution ruling's separate scope. Paragraphs 26-28 affirm and deny appellate sanctions, accurately attributed to the reviewing court.

Cover names Edward Arce as circuit judge; Oden Johnson authored the appellate opinion with Mikva and Tailor. Correct trial-versus-appellate attribution. Paragraph 17 and footnote 5 confirm the actual trial ruling struck section 904, the savings provision, as applied even though the motion initially challenged section 607 in conjunction with section 904. The ledger uses the correct savings-provision description. Paragraphs 34-37, 40-44 and 51-54 support the distinction between no express statutory right under the 1984 Act and a merely possible equitable extension. The appellate court reversed on nonconstitutional grounds and did not decide the wider due-process question. The ledger does not misstate the remand as a final paternity adjudication.

Ryan is the trial judge for the reviewed October 17 detention order. The earlier erroneous order is distinguished. The published appellate affirmance and Ellis concurrence are separate from her action. Reader checked all opinion paragraphs, including concurrence.
The breath-test exclusion and directed finding concern one DUI count; the other impairment DUI conviction was affirmed. The appeal did not challenge the two traffic counts.

The refusal to continue the trial and later new-trial denial belong to Walowski. The reviewing court reversed for failure to consider continuance factors and resulting prejudice, without reaching remaining alleged errors.
Walowski denied the new-trial motion because the new witness arrived after the shooting and was insufficiently conclusive. The appellate court affirmed that selected ruling.

Caption identifies Kyriakopoulos. The September 5, 2014 dismissal predates Jesinoski. Affirmance is limited to original-disclosure damages; rescission defense and failure-to-honor-rescission damages were restored. Paragraph 9 and footnote 2 say the circuit court did not separately address the latter counterclaim.

Caption identifies Kyriakopoulos. Summary judgment rejected additional interest and attorney fees after the award was paid. The ledger expressly assigns the bond rationale to the appellate court rather than inventing trial reasoning.

Caption identifies Moreland. She compelled arbitration and stayed litigation. Appellate reversal rests on the individual not being a signatory or intended beneficiary; the trial rationale is not reported, accurately disclosed.

Caption identifies Carroll and Lampkin as the reviewing justice. This was a civil summary-suspension proceeding. Record inadequacy and alternative police-report evidence support affirmance without deciding the contested video foundation.

Caption identifies Carroll. He found guilt after a bench trial; the appellate court rejected the unpreserved medical-evidence claim after no-error review and reversed the separate failure-to-yield conviction for missing statutory proof. Both outcomes are disclosed.

Caption identifies Buford. The trial court separately found unfitness and best interests. The appellate court affirmed statutory depravity and best interests without reaching alternate unfitness grounds. Ledger avoids reproducing personal details.
